title: Add a Health Check to a Shiny App — add_healthcheck
text: Registers one healthcheck endpoints Shiny app decorating app object's internal HTTP handler. Requests matching registered path (via GET) answered handler UI rendering, session creation, authentication occurs; requests fall app unchanged. interception happens app object's handler, uiPattern adjustment required endpoint works regardless app constructed (plain shiny::shinyApp(), golem, UI wrappers, etc.). Registrations stack: call add_healthcheck() multiple times different paths expose e.g. separate liveness (/livez) readiness (/readyz) endpoints handlers.

text: status Character string reported body status field. Default "pass". ... Additional named fields merged response body top level (e.g. version, description, output). checks Optional named list check results, serialized body's checks field. Elements may arbitrarily nested lists; structure interpreted. status_code Integer HTTP status code 100 599. Default 200L. timestamp Character timestamp body's timestamp field. Default ts_utc(). headers Named list HTTP headers merged defaults (caller wins). content_type MIME type response. Default "application/health+json". body Named list representing structured response body (low-level constructor). x object coerce test. arg argument name string. argument mentioned error messages input origin problem. call execution environment currently running function, e.g. caller_env(). function mentioned error messages source error. See call argument abort() information.

title: Health Check Response — health_response
text: health_response(), new_health_response(), as_health_response() return health_response object (classed shiny::httpResponse()). validate_health_response() invisibly returns input valid, otherwise throws check_error condition. is_health_response() returns logical scalar.

title: Health Check Response — health_response
text: HTTP transport status (status_code) body status field deliberately independent: Orchestrators load balancers (Kubernetes, Cloud Run, Azure Container Apps, etc.) interpret HTTP status code: codes >= 200 < 400 indicate success, anything else indicates failure. body status string convention humans tooling. default value ("pass") follows IETF health check response format draft (draft-inadarei-api-health-check, also suggests "warn" "fail"), value accepted – use whatever vocabulary fits conventions. defaults compose healthy response (status = "pass", status_code = 200L). unhealthy response, 503L (Service Unavailable) standard choice, typically paired status = "fail". individual checks aggregate overall status intentionally decided – policy belongs handler builds response.

title: Health Check Response — health_response
text: Default headers Cache-Control: -store (RFC 9111) probe responses never cached. legacy Pragma/Expires response headers deprecated RFC 9111 intentionally omitted. CORS headers sent default (probes server--server); supply via headers browser client another origin needs access. default content type application/health+json per IETF draft. +json structured syntax suffix (RFC 6839) guarantees JSON processor handles ; use content_type override (e.g. plain application/json). Timestamps use RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 format UTC (see ts_utc()).

title: Health Check Response — health_response
code: # healthy response with defaults health_response()  # unhealthy response (standard choice: 503 + "fail") health_response(status = "fail", status_code = 503L)  # custom vocabulary, extra fields, and nested checks health_response(   status = "HEALTHY",   version = "1.0.0",   checks = list(     database = list(status = "pass", latency_ms = 2.3),     api = list(status = "warn", output = "slow response times")   ) )
